subject: Exec update: Quantization Profile Library (cost optimization) — impact, risks, resourcing ask
body:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 8:42 AM
Subject: Exec update: Quantization Profile Library (cost optimization) — impact, risks, resourcing ask

Attached is a 2-pager for leadership review ahead of next week’s operating review.

TL;DR
- We’re on track to ship an opt-in Quantization Profile Library with route-scoped enablement (Hosted first; Dedicated/Private validation in parallel).
- Expected unit cost impact (initial model set, conservative):
  - INT8 profiles: ~15–25% lower $/1M tokens at similar p50 latency.
  - INT4 profiles (where quality gates pass): ~30–45% lower $/1M tokens, with higher workload sensitivity.
- Primary risks are quality regressions (JSON/tool-calling), hardware/kernel compatibility, and operational safety (bad scoping / misconfig).
- We have mitigation in place (quality gates + canary + auto-rollback + signed artifacts) but we need a small, time-bound cross-team resourcing push to hit the beta window.

Cost impact (what we’re telling the business)
- Near-term: improve gross margin on high-volume summarization/embedding-adjacent generation routes and provide a credible “cost lever” for sales with safety controls.
- Initial target: beta with 2–3 high-traffic model families; route-scoped opt-in only. No default-on.

Risk mitigation (how we keep this safe)
- Route-level enablement + canary (start at 1–5% traffic) with fast rollback.
- Strict profile scoping (model version + GPU arch + kernel constraints); runtime falls back to baseline on incompatibility.
- Quality gates prior to publish (prompt sets include long-context + JSON mode + tool-calling). Reject profiles with regressions beyond thresholds.
- Signed profile artifacts + audit logs for all config changes.

Timeline (proposed)
- Wk 1–2 (now): PRD/design/spec final + initial model list locked; hardware matrix agreed.
- Wk 3–6: registry artifacts + runtime resolution + route policy controls behind feature flags.
- Wk 5–8: eval/perf pipeline + dashboards + rollback tooling; begin beta onboarding.
- Wk 9–10: Dedicated/Private compatibility testing; docs/SDK guidance.
- Wk 11–12: limited beta → GA decision based on KPIs (cost savings + regression rate + rollback frequency).

Asks / resourcing (to stay on schedule)
1) Runtime/Kernel: 1 additional engineer for 4 weeks to close the GPU/kernel compatibility matrix + long-context perf issues (Mateo/Hiro teams are stretched).
2) SRE: 0.5–1 engineer for 3 weeks to formalize alerting + auto-disable hooks (quality regression → route disable).
3) Security: a scheduled review slot in the next 2 weeks for artifact signing/verification + publish permissions (avoid late-cycle block).

If you’re aligned, I’ll have Talia coordinate the resource commitments with Eng leads and bring a crisp go/no-go checklist to the operating review.

Thanks,
Ava

—
Ava Chen
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: QuantProfiles_ExecUpdate_CostImpact_RiskTimeline_v3.pdf


From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Exec update: Quantization Profile Library (cost optimization) — impact, risks, resourcing ask

This is helpful.

Two questions we’ll likely get from leadership:
1) What’s the adoption assumption behind the cost savings? (i.e., if it’s opt-in + route-scoped, do we have a plan to actually drive usage?)
2) What are the hard “no-go” thresholds for beta/GA? I want something concrete beyond “quality regressions.”

On resourcing: I support the runtime + SRE asks if we can keep them time-boxed and tied to the beta deliverables.

- Aditya


From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 1:18 PM
Subject: Re: Exec update: Quantization Profile Library (cost optimization) — impact, risks, resourcing ask

+1 on getting the security review scheduled early.

From what I’m seeing, the things that will bite us if we hand-wave them:
- Artifact integrity: we need signing + verification in runtime (not just “signed in registry”), plus an audit trail for who published what.
- Access control: publish permissions for Applied ML must be least-privilege and tied to an approval workflow (even if lightweight).
- Operational auditability: route config changes should be attributable (who/when) and reversible.

If you can send me the current assumptions (signing approach, where verification happens, and how publish auth works), I’ll get a review meeting on the calendar this week.

Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference


From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 4:09 PM
Subject: Re: Exec update: Quantization Profile Library (cost optimization) — impact, risks, resourcing ask

Replying inline.

On Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 10:06 AM Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> 1) What’s the adoption assumption behind the cost savings?

For the exec narrative I’m proposing we separate “platform capability” from “realized savings.”
- Beta: success = capability shipped + 3–5 design partners enabled on 1–2 routes each, with measured savings and no sustained regressions.
- Post-beta: adoption motion = Redwood Optimize recommendations + Console nudges (route-level) + solutions engineering playbook for batch workloads.

Assumption for the initial cost model (conservative):
- 10–15% of eligible tokens in Hosted shift to INT8 within ~60 days post-beta (mostly summarization/background routes).
- INT4 remains smaller in early days (workload-dependent; expect 3–5% of eligible tokens until we expand prompt sets + confidence).

> 2) What are the hard “no-go” thresholds for beta/GA?

Proposed no-go for beta (opt-in only):
- Any repeatable regression in JSON mode / tool-calling format adherence above our guardrail thresholds on the quantization prompt set.
- Any hardware scoping issue that causes elevated 5xx on a GPU class (even if fallback works sometimes).
- Any inability to attribute cost correctly (quantized vs baseline) in telemetry/billing tags.

Proposed GA gates (for expanding availability, still opt-in):
- Sustained cost improvement ≥ 15% on at least one high-volume route type with p95 latency neutral-to-better.
- Regression rate low enough that auto-disable triggers are rare and explainable (we’ll put an explicit target in the go/no-go doc).
- Audit logs + signing verification fully in place and validated.

Naomi — I’ll send a short summary of current assumptions tonight, but quick answers:
- Signing: registry stores signed profile artifacts; runtime verifies signature at fetch time and caches only verified blobs.
- Publish auth: internal publish API w/ RBAC; Applied ML publish requests require reviewer approval (lightweight workflow). We’ll make sure the audit log includes publisher + approver.

Talia: can you please draft a 1-pager resourcing plan with (a) named asks, (b) duration, (c) deliverables, and (d) what slips if we don’t get it?

Ava

—
Ava Chen
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
